description: SYNTHETIC HELD-OUT test collection. 'Yusuf Ali' is a fictional persona. Written on 2026-11-13 AFTER the first evaluation on the Fatima development set but BEFORE any retrieval change motivated by that evaluation, and not used for any tuning. See eval/README.md.

documents.title: Maryam
documents.text: Your wife. You have been married for fifty-two years. She makes the best halwa.

documents.title: Tariq
documents.text: Your elder son. He runs the family cloth shop in the bazaar.

documents.title: Ayesha
documents.text: Your daughter. She is a nurse in Rawalpindi and visits every second weekend.

documents.title: Omar
documents.text: Your grandson, Tariq's boy. He is fourteen and plays cricket for his school.

documents.title: Haji Nazir
documents.text: Your oldest friend. You play ludo with him at the tea stall.

documents.title: Sister Parveen
documents.text: Your sister. She lives in Mirpur and sends mangoes every summer.

documents.title: The cloth shop
documents.text: The shop you opened in 1972 in the main bazaar. Tariq runs it now.

documents.title: Jhelum river bank
documents.text: Where you liked to sit in the evening and watch the boats.

documents.title: Ayesha's hospital
documents.text: The hospital in Rawalpindi where Ayesha works.

documents.title: Wedding to Maryam
documents.text: You married Maryam in Jhelum. Her father gave you his watch.

documents.title: Opening the shop
documents.text: The first day of the cloth shop. Haji Nazir brought sweets.

documents.title: Omar's first cricket trophy
documents.text: Omar won best bowler in the school tournament.

documents.title: Trip to Murree
documents.text: The family holiday in the hills. It snowed and Ayesha built a snowman.

documents.title: Fajr and morning walk
documents.text: Dawn prayer, then a walk to the end of the lane.

documents.title: Newspaper
documents.text: Maryam reads the Urdu newspaper to you with breakfast.

documents.title: Tea stall with Nazir
documents.text: Ludo and tea with Haji Nazir.

documents.title: Evening pills
documents.text: Take the white tablet with dinner. Maryam keeps them in the kitchen drawer.

documents.title: Cricket on television
documents.text: Watch the match highlights with Omar.

documents.title: My walking stick
documents.text: The walnut stick from Kashmir stands behind the front door.

documents.title: Favourite poet
documents.text: Allama Iqbal. I know many of his verses by heart.

documents.title: My old job
documents.text: Before the shop I was a clerk at the railway station for six years.

documents.title: Maryam and me on our anniversary
The front of our cloth shop
